column1: # The parity matrix of Desk Tables: every row of the survey of Numbers '09,
# each with the phase of the roadmap of Desk Tables that completes it
# (- when out of scope). The shared column names the rows of the other
# surveys that describe the same feature, or says the feature is only
# of Numbers. The NGNM rows are what the GNOME HIG and desktop ask, and
# the NVMI rows are the commands that the inventory of Numbers on the
# reference virtual machine added to the survey.
# Tab-separated; the survey, the roadmap and the inventory of 2026-11-14
# The gnome column says how Desk adapts a row to GNOME where the
# and interface B of docs/interface) changed its form; the row passes
# when Desk does it that way.

column4: expected
column8: gnome

column4: Categories (Blank, Personal Finance and others), icons that run through the template when the pointer rests on them, a size control, Open an Existing File and Recent. Remembers the last category and template chosen.
column8: A template gallery inside the empty window, without a window of its own, as in Desk Writer (path E)

column4: Sheets pane at the top left, Styles pane below it, instant calculation area, toolbar, format bar, formula bar and the sheet canvas.
column8: Interface B: the sheets, with the tables and charts of each, are in the navigation sidebar; table styles in the Inspector and on a page of the sidebar; instant calculation in the bottom bar; the formula bar under the format bar

column4: Lists the sheets and, within each, only the tables and charts. Collapses by sheet. Clicking an item selects the object and shows it on the canvas, and the item being edited is highlighted.
column8: Interface B: the Sheets page of the navigation sidebar, with the Add button in its header

column4: View > Zoom and a menu at the bottom left corner. In Print View, a smaller zoom shows more pages.
column8: Interface B: zoom button at the start of the bottom bar, besides the View menu

column4: Shows the sheet divided into pages, with header and footer areas, orientation buttons and a content scale control. The details are in the section on printing.
View > Enter Full Screen or the button at the corner of the window. Esc leaves.
column8: F11 enters and leaves full screen

column4: Customizable as in Pages. Default buttons: Sheet, Table, Reorganize (sort, filter and categorize), Function, Chart, Text Box, Shape, Comment, Share, Formula List, View, Full Screen, Inspector, Media, Colors and Fonts.
column8: A lean header bar, without customization (decision of 13 November, path A). In interface B, chosen on 14 November, it is the same as in Desk Writer: the Sidebar button with the View menu, Insert and the Table, Chart, Text box, Shape, Media and Comment buttons at the start; Search, Inspector and the main menu at the end. Sheet moves to the Add button of the sidebar, Function to the formula bar and Reorganize to the Data tab of the Inspector

column4: Changes with the selection. With a table or cell: show the table name, cell text, value format, borders, headers and footers, alignment and background color.
column8: Interface B: a lean bar with font, size, bold, italic, underline, text color, alignment, data format, decimal places, fill, borders and More; the rest is in the Inspector

column4: Document, Sheet, Table, Cells, Chart, Text, Graphic, Metrics, Hyperlink and QuickTime. Several windows can be open. Sheet and Cells take the place of the Layout and Wrap panes of Pages.
column8: A single Inspector, in the sidebar, as in Desk Writer (path C). In interface B the first level is Format, Data and Document: Format has the tabs of what is selected (table: Table, Cell, Text and Arrange; chart: Chart, Axis, Series and Arrange), Data has Sort, Filter and Categories, and Document has Sheet and Info

column4: Always visible. Shows and edits the formula or content of the selected cell, with Accept, Cancel, text size and the Function Browser button.
column8: Interface B: under the format bar, with the active cell, the Function button and the content field; Cancel and Accept appear while editing

column4: The editor opens when = is typed in a cell and can be dragged. The browser lists the functions by category, with search, a description and Insert. The details are in the section on formulas.
Lists the table styles of the template. With a table selected, a click changes its appearance.
column8: Interface B: table styles at the top of the Table tab of the Inspector and on the Table styles page of the navigation sidebar

column4: With two or more cells selected, even if not adjacent, the bottom left corner shows sum, average, minimum, maximum and count. Dragging a result into a cell writes the formula.
column8: Interface B: the results appear as chips in the bottom bar, which can be dragged into a cell

column4: The same as in Pages.
column8: Media as a popover of the Media button, Fonts and Colors as popovers, as in Desk Writer (path D and interface B)

column4: Lists what was not imported or exported correctly. Lets the user replace a missing font and copy the warnings.
column8: A banner with See warnings and the list in a dialog, as in Desk Writer (path I)

column4: A list of shortcuts in Help. Control-click opens the context menu, much used in tables and charts.
column8: Context menu from the right button, the Menu key and Shift+F10; the GNOME shortcuts dialog

column4: Onscreen help, video tutorials, help tags when the pointer rests, and the iWork formulas and functions guides in the Help menu.
column8: Help in the GNOME format, opened with F1

column4: The Blank template, without formatting. A preference to always open a chosen template instead of the Chooser.
Excel and AppleWorks 6 (spreadsheets only), by dragging onto the app icon or with File > Open. If that fails, the guide suggests saving in another format or copying and pasting.

column3: Import CSV, tab-delimited text and OFX
column4: Opening the file creates a new document. Dragged onto the canvas, it creates one or more tables. In an empty table, it fills it and creates the missing columns. In a table with data, it appends the rows and, if the columns do not match, asks whether to cancel, add columns, ignore the extra ones or create a new table.
From the Chooser (Open an Existing File and Recent), with File > Open, a double click or dragging onto the icon. Opens iWork '08 and '09 documents.
The document opens with substitute fonts. Missing movies and sounds have to be inserted again.

The same as in Pages, with the Password Assistant, an option to keep it in the Keychain and a hint shown after two wrong tries. Does not apply to copies in iWork '08 or Excel, and the exported PDF has its own password.
Automatic saving, "Include preview in document" (also as a preference) and a copy in iWork '08 or Excel. Advanced options: copy audio and movies and copy template images. Fonts do not go in the file.
column8: A recovery draft in place of Lion automatic saving (path L)

column4: Unlimited undo since opening and File > Revert to Saved.
Prevents accidental editing until the user unlocks it, from the window title menu.
Cmd-S keeps a version. "Browse All Versions" restores the whole document or lets the user copy objects and settings. The "Backup of" preference keeps only the previous version.
column8: A recovery draft in place of the Lion versions (path L)

column4: Creates an untitled copy opened next to the original.
The template then appears in My Templates in the Chooser.
Author and keywords in the Document Inspector, used by the system search.
With Option, closes all. Asks to save if there are changes.
column8: The question "Save changes?" with Cancel | Discard | Save, as in GNOME

column4: Reading and writing the original format is a requirement, but the guide does not describe it. The specification comes from outside sources and tests on the VM, as for .pages.
Divide the document like chapters. Each sheet is a free canvas with tables, charts and other objects, and the pane lists only the tables and charts.
column7: Extension: a sheet with several tables

column4: The Sheet button creates, at the end of the list, a sheet with a predefined table. Copy with Option-drag, Duplicate or copy and paste. Delete deletes the sheet with its content.
Drag one or several sheets in the pane, cut and paste sheets and move tables and charts between sheets. The order of the items in the pane does not change their position on the canvas.
Double click in the pane or the Name field of the Sheet Inspector.
The Tables button or Insert > Table, with the predefined types of the template. Dragging cells, a row or a column onto the canvas creates a new table, and with Option the original stays.

Format bar, Table Inspector (name, 1 to 5 headers and footers, merge and split, sizes, borders, background and the behavior of Return and Tab), Cells Inspector (formats and conditional formatting), Graphic Inspector for shadows, table styles and the context menu.
With a cell selected the column letters and row numbers appear, used in formulas, each tab with a menu. Handles to move the table, add columns, add rows and both at once on the diagonal.
Handles with Shift and Option, exact size and position in the Metrics Inspector. Dragging by the edge or the handle moves, Shift constrains to 0°, 45° and 90°, and Option-drag copies.
Every table has a name (Table 1, Table 2...), unique in the sheet. It appears in the pane and, if turned on, above the table, with its own text formatting and an adjustable space to the body.
Table or cell background with color, gradient or image, borders and text. Copy Style and Paste Style.

Format > Advanced > Capture Table keeps structure, style and content in the Tables menu, with the option to use the default style of the document. Formulas can only refer to the table itself. Manage Tables renames, reorders and deletes. Applies to the document, or to new documents if it becomes a template.

column3: Copy a table to another application
column4: Keeps appearance, data and attributes, but removes hidden rows and columns and does not copy cell comments.

A table from the pane, the edge or with Cmd-Return. A cell, a range, loose cells with Cmd, rows and columns from the tabs. Borders from the Borders button or in the Allow Border Selection mode, with a single or long segment.

column3: Navigation and "Return key moves to next cell"
column4: The same rules as in Pages for Tab, Shift-Tab, arrows, Return and Shift-Return. At the end of the table, Tab and Return create a column or a row, as the option says.
When rows and columns are inserted, deleted, resized, hidden or shown, nearby objects move so as not to overlap. A preference turns it off.

Option with the arrows, the tab menu, the Table menu (as many as selected), Return or Tab at the end, and handles. New rows go above the footer and repeat the formula or cell control that repeats through the whole column. With a filter on, rows cannot be added.
column8: Alt and the arrows insert a row above or below and a column before or after, like Option and the arrows in Numbers

column3: Move and copy rows and columns
column4: Dragging the reference tab moves the row or column within the table or to another table. With Option, copies.
The Table menu, the tab menu and handles. Dragging the handle inward deletes empty rows or columns, and with Option also those that have content.

Up to 5 header rows and 5 header columns and 5 footer rows, from the bar, the Inspector, the Table menu or by converting the first row or column of the body. The corner belongs to the row header. In Print View, headers can repeat on each page.
Outside Print View, header rows and columns stay visible when scrolling. It is an option of each table.
column7: Partial: ODS freezes the sheet, not the table

column4: Distribute evenly (even if not adjacent), exact height and width, Fit to content or a double click on the separator of the tabs, and dragging borders.
Bands in the chosen color, and the other rows use the cell background.

From the tab menu, one or several. Show all, only the neighbors or those of the range. The numbering of the tabs shows the gap. Formulas and sorting keep using the hidden cells, and rows or columns with merged cells cannot be hidden.

From the column tab, ascending or descending, or in the Reorganize window: the whole table or selected rows, several columns in sequence, and Sort Now to reorder after editing. The order by type is the same as in Pages.

The Reorganize window: rules per column, which add up, including "is in the top n" or "bottom n", which can show more than n rows. Rows outside the filter are hidden. Turning off "Show rows that match" brings everything back.
Group rows under a category row with a triangle to collapse. Created by hand (Insert Category, Create Category from Selected Rows) or from the values of a column (Categorize by This Column).
column7: Partial: approximated with row groups and subtotals

column4: When created by hand, a new column keeps a provisional name per category. By column, each unique value becomes a category, and changing the value moves the row. Renaming the category row rewrites the column. Dates are grouped by unit, such as year. A deleted value takes the row to the blank category, and a category without rows goes away.
Subcategories from the Reorganize window, Add Category Above or Below, promote and demote levels, move categories by the tab and move rows between categories.
Turn all off for a while (Table > Turn Off All Categories) and back on, or delete by level or by column.

The formatting of one applies to all of the same level. Each cell can show Subtotal, Average and other numeric calculations (without dates and durations), Count of non-empty cells, the category name or nothing, with the function name optional. New rows inherit the values of the category. Expand and collapse by level, or everything with Option-click.

Typing replaces, a double click edits a part, and Return or Enter selects everything when the Return option is off. Esc undoes what was typed since the selection, Delete deletes and Clear All removes content, background and style.

Autocomplete with values of the table (a preference), Option-Return for a line break, Return for a paragraph when the option is off and Option-Tab for a tab. Horizontal alignment, including "align text left and numbers right", and vertical. Spelling and find and replace work in cells.
Takes digits and + − ( ) / currency % . E and e. Long decimals are rounded, large integers go to scientific notation, and what still does not fit is cut. Numeric functions ignore text.

The fill handle copies value, format, formula and background, without comments. Fill right, left, up and down. Continues weekdays, months and progressions from two cells, without creating a link between them.

A cut number or date shows an indicator. With "Wrap Text in Cell" off, text overflows into empty neighbors, but numbers and dates never overflow. Fit buttons for width and height. The row height follows the content, and the width does not.

As in Pages: rules for numbers, text and dates, a fixed value or a reference to a cell of any table, text color, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and fill, and the highest rule wins for each attribute. Select All with the same rules, Clear All Rules and copy rules to another table.
Color, gradient or image, from the Table Inspector.
As in Pages. Rows and columns with merged cells cannot be hidden.
Style (or none), thickness and color per segment, from the bar or the Inspector.

Dragging moves and replaces, Option-dragging copies, in the same table, to another or onto the canvas. A copied cell can be pasted into several loose cells. Insert > Copied Columns or Copied Rows makes room instead of overwriting. The comment goes with the content and goes away when the content is deleted.

The Comment button or Insert > Comment. The box can be moved, and when hidden becomes a yellow marker that shows the text when the pointer rests on it. Show and hide all, delete, and print the visible ones.

Automatic, Number, Currency, Percentage, Date and Time, Duration, Fraction, Numeral System, Scientific, Text, controls and custom ones. The format only changes the display, the formula bar shows the real value and deleting the value keeps the format.

Recognizes number, currency (0 or 2 places), date in the system format (a 2-digit year above 50 becomes 19xx), boolean (TRUE and FALSE), percentage, scientific (2 places) and duration with the suffixes w, d, h, m, s and ms. A fraction that looks like a date becomes a date.

Rounded decimal places, style of negatives and thousands separator, with buttons in the bar. Currency has a symbol, the full list of currencies by a preference, and the accounting style, which puts the symbol against the edge. In Percentage, a 3 already typed becomes 300%.

column3: Date and time, duration and fraction
column4: Date and time from lists of formats. Duration chooses the units on a slider (from weeks to milliseconds, with h, m and s by default) and the display style. Fraction by precision, such as up to three digits, halves or eighths.
column7: Partial: duration in weeks and days

column4: Bases from 2 to 36 with the number of digits. In bases 2, 8 and 16, negatives with a sign or in two's complement. Scientific with decimal places.
Shows exactly what was typed, numbers too.

Checkbox (checked or not), slider (minimum, maximum, increment, position on the right or below, format and places), stepper (minimum, maximum, increment, format and places) and pop-up menu with an editable list, in which numbers stay numbers. The checkbox and menu change only through the control, and the other two also take typing.
column7: Partial: menu as a validation list, the rest by extension

column4: As in Pages: Integers, Currency, Decimals (or fraction), Spaces (normal, wide, thin and flexible) and Scale elements, fixed text, conditions by value and the Typed Text element. If the format with scale is applied before typing, the scale changes the stored value.
Built from elements and fixed text and applied when the typed value has a hyphen or a slash.
Show Format to edit and replace or save under another name. Rename, reorder and delete. Old cells keep the old name until they are reassigned.

Defines the table background (color or image, with opacity), stroke, color and opacity of the outer borders of the body, the header row and column and the footer, and the background and text of the cells of each area. The templates bring several in the Styles pane.

Changes made after applying are overrides. Clicking the style or dragging it onto the table changes the style and keeps the overrides, and Clear and Apply Style (or Reapply Table Style) removes them. Dragging a style onto the icon of a sheet applies it to all its tables.
column7: Partial: link between table and style

column4: Background from the fill well or the Table Inspector, opacity from the Graphic Inspector, borders and text from the usual controls. Redefine Style from Table updates all tables with the style and keeps their overrides.
column7: Partial: link between table and style

column4: Copy Style and Paste Style of cells. Paste and Match Style pastes a table with the default style of the document.
Set as Default Style for New Tables. Reusable tables can use the default style instead of their own.
Create New Style from the table, with a name unique in the document. Deleting a style in use asks for another to replace it. New styles only go to other documents through a template.
Starts with =, has constants (number and text), references, operators and functions. When an operator is missing, the editor inserts + by itself.

Arithmetic + − * / ^ and % after the number (A2% is 0.2). Comparison = <> > < >= <=, which returns TRUE or FALSE. & joins text. Text is greater than a number, TRUE and FALSE compare only with each other (TRUE = 1 gives FALSE) and text with an arithmetic operator gives an error. Wildcards ? * and ~ in conditions.
Sum, average, minimum, maximum and count (numbers, dates and times) of the selected cells. Dragging a result into an empty cell of any table creates the formula.

Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, Count and Product. Cells of a column put the result in the first empty cell below, or in a new row; of a row, in the first empty cell to the right, or in a new column. The whole column puts the result in the footer, created if needed, and the whole row in a new column.

Opens with =, a double click on a formula, the Function button, Insert > Function or Option-Return, over the cell, and can be dragged. Return, Enter, Accept or clicking outside saves, and Esc or Cancel discards. References and functions appear as tokens.
Edits the formula of the selected cell, with text size, a height that can be dragged or fitted to the content with a double click, Accept and Cancel.

Categories, All in alphabetical order, Recent (the last ten), search and description. The function goes in with argument placeholders: optional ones in gray, help when the pointer rests and a list of valid values for arguments with fixed options.
A blue triangle at the corner of the cell for a warning and a red one in the middle for an error, with the message on a click. A preference warns when a formula refers to empty cells.
Cell (C55), range (B2:B5), whole row (1:1), whole column (C), range of rows (2:6) and of columns (B:C).

2006 Revenue crosses the 2006 column with the Revenue row, and a header merged over several columns refers to all of them. With several header rows, the nearest name counts, unless it repeats in another header. A preference turns on insertion by name and the suggestions after three letters.
column7: Extension: the name kept with the A1 reference

column3: References to other tables and sheets
column4: Table 2::B5 and Sheet 2::Table 2::Name. Table and sheet can be left out when the name is unique in the document. Insertion with the mouse in another table, or from the keyboard with Option-Cmd-Page Up and Page Down.
column7: Partial: depends on how tables map to ODS sheets

column4: $ on the row, the column or both, from the reference menu or with Cmd-K. Moving the formula keeps the references, and copy and paste adjusts the relative ones. Moving the formula and the cells it refers to together keeps the formula, and moving a referenced cell updates the reference.
Paste Values pastes only the result. Mark for Move and then Move take the formula to a cell out of view.
A window with the location (sheet and table), result and formula of all the formulas of the document, with search. A click shows the cell, and a double click edits it.
column8: Interface B: the Formula list page of the navigation sidebar, opened with Ctrl+Shift+F (Ctrl+Alt+F already opens the search results)

column4: The Formulas Only option, with match case, whole words, repeat, next, previous, replace, replace all and replace and find. The Formula Editor opens at each match.
262 functions in 10 categories, the same in the three applications (table below).
column7: Partial: 10 functions without an equivalent in OpenFormula

column4: Column, stacked column, bar, stacked bar, line, area, stacked area, pie, scatter, mixed and 2-axis. All but scatter, mixed and 2-axis also in 3D.
As in Pages. On creation, rows become series if the table is square or wider than tall, and the header text becomes labels.

A chart of the whole table, a range, loose cells (Cmd) or several tables. Without a selection, it starts with a new table of sample data, visible on the sheet. Option-click draws the chart. When a cell changes, the chart updates.

With the chart selected, a dark frame marks the cells used, with a square of the color of each series and the button that swaps rows and columns. In scatter, the button becomes a gear with "Share X Values".

Shift- or Cmd-click on cells, drag the round control of the range (two by two in scatter), insert rows or columns within the range, or drag cells of another table onto the chart, creating a series. Deleting the value of the cell removes it from the chart and the table. Shrinking the range or deleting the series or the category label removes it only from the chart.
Show Hidden Data includes or excludes hidden rows and columns.

column3: Order, data and label of each series
column4: In the Series pane: position of the series, a Data field with the cell range and a Label field with the name cell. Changing the series does not change the table.

Moving on the same sheet, or cutting and pasting on another, keeps the link to the cells. Deleting the chart keeps the tables, and deleting the source tables deletes the chart too (to be checked on the VM).
With the document saved, copying and pasting in Pages or Keynote creates a linked chart. Refresh rereads the saved document, and Unlink cuts the link.
As in Pages: pie uses the first value of each series, scatter needs pairs and ignores the last odd row or column, the common attributes stay and the specific ones go back to the default.
As in Pages. The legend labels come from the cells or are edited in the legend. Text boxes can be grouped with the chart.
As in Pages: 2D rotates and 3D does not. In a group, only the 2D ones rotate.

As in Pages: gridlines, tick marks, maximum and minimum (Auto), steps, labels, minimum value, number format with a suffix, category labels by reference to cells, a label every N categories, last category and titles. Linear or logarithmic scale in non-stacked 2D, percentage in stacked 2D and only linear in 3D.
As in Pages: collections of colors and textures, Apply All or drag onto a series, opacity of the whole chart or of the series fill, stroke and shadow. Value labels with their own position and format.
As in Pages, with X and Y bars in scatter and an equation and R² that can be dragged.

As in Pages: only the first data set, selection of wedges, colors and textures per wedge, labels with a distance from the center, series name, exploded wedges, individual or group shadow and rotation angle.
As in Pages: gap between bars and between sets, shadows and series names; symbols with size and a straight or curved line; X and Y pairs, shared X and separate colors for points, line and trend.
As in Pages: each series as a column, line or area, with Y1 and Y2 axes.
As in Pages, plus the bar shape in 3D column and bar charts.
In text boxes, shapes, cells, page headers and footers, comments and charts. There is no body text and no flow of pages.

Always floating. The height follows the text, the width changes with the handles (narrowing forces the height), Option-click draws the box and Cmd-Return leaves editing. Columns in boxes and rectangles. The guide does not mention linked boxes.

Font, size, color, bold, italic, underline, shadow, strikethrough, outline, baseline, capitals, smoothing, alignments, spacing, background color, tabs, indents and inset. There are no paragraph, character or list styles, nor a Styles Drawer.

Bulleted, numbered and ordered from the Text Inspector, and automatic detection when typing •, *, - or a number, letter or Roman numeral with a period. Tab and Shift-Tab change the level. In a cell where Return goes to the next one, Option-Return is used.
Page number, page count, date and time (updated on open) and file name (with optional path and extension), in any text, not only in headers and footers.

To a webpage and to an email message with recipient and subject. Typed addresses become links (a preference of the computer), and "Make all links inactive" lets the user edit the text. The guide does not mention links to bookmarks or other documents.
As in Pages: smart quotes, capitals at the start of a sentence, superscript ordinals, substitutions, nonbreaking space, spell checking with suggestions, accents and keyboards.

A find window with a list of results, Match Case, Whole Words and the last ten searches. Find and Replace in the whole document or only in the current sheet, and matches in formulas open the Formula Editor.
As in Pages: QuickTime formats (TIFF, GIF, JPEG, PDF, PSD, EPS and PICT), media placeholders in templates, rectangular or shaped mask, Instant Alpha, Adjust Image and file reduction.
As in Pages: predefined, drawn with the pen, edit points and parametric shapes (rounded rectangle, arrows, callout, star and polygon).
As in Pages, with a frame on movies and playback controls.
As in Pages, but without inline objects, text wrap or master objects: selection, copy, layers, alignment, guides, group, connection line, lock, resize, rotate and flip.
As in Pages: borders, frames, shadow, reflection, opacity and fills with color, gradient and image.
MathType 6, then treated as an image.

More than 60 names with synonyms: name parts, nickname, job title, department, company, phones, emails, URLs, birthday, AIM, Yahoo, work, home and other addresses, and note. The "first available" fields use the first value of the card.
If the header row uses field names, dragging cards, groups or vCards adds a row per contact, even if repeated. Fields without a matching column are left out.
Dragging cards, a group or vCards onto the canvas creates a table with a column per field. Only Last Name, First Name, Phone and Email are visible, and the other columns are hidden.
The Numbers table feeds the Pages merge fields, each field linked to a column header (IOP-03).
Shows the sheet in pages. Objects can be moved and resized between pages, and long tables split across them. The zoom sets how many pages appear.

In the Sheet Inspector: content scale (also from a control at the corner of the window), orientation, page order (top to bottom or left to right), starting number or continuing from the previous sheet, margins and header and footer distance.
One for the document, in the Document Inspector.
Text and fields (page number, page count, date and file name) at the top and foot of each page of the sheet, seen in Print View or with Show Layout.
Header rows and columns repeat on each page when the table splits, which can be turned off in the Table menu.
Ignores the margins of the Inspector and uses the largest printable area.
Printer, copies, collate, all sheets or only the current one, and an option to print the list of all the formulas of the document.

Image quality (72 dpi, 150 dpi or no reduction), Sheet layout (each sheet on one page) or Page layout (the pagination of Print View), and passwords to open, print and copy, of up to 32 ASCII characters.

Each table becomes an Excel worksheet. With more than one table, the other objects go to separate worksheets, and a summary worksheet is optional. The guide warns that some calculations may give a different result in Excel. Also available from Save As > Save a copy as.
One file per table, all in a folder, with the last calculated values and without charts. UTF-8, Mac OS Roman or Windows Latin 1 encoding.
Share with guests, publish or keep for private use.
column7: Out of scope: service shut down

column4: Attaches the document as Numbers (with the password), Excel or PDF.
Attaches the document as Numbers or PDF to a blog or podcast.
Linked charts, copied tables and contact data for mail merge, as page 243 sums up.
Table styles, reusable tables, the default style of each chart type, of text box, shape and image, the number and names of the sheets and the starting content.
Table styles and the Tables menu travel with the template.
Format > Advanced > Define Default Style, repeated for each chart type.

column3: Default text box, shape and image
column4: Fill, stroke, shadow, opacity and text of boxes and shapes. Shadow, opacity, borders, mask and adjustments of imported images.
Table names, chart and axis titles, formulas, cell formats and controls, text boxes and comments with instructions and highlight colors.
A formatted image, sound or movie marked with Define as Media Placeholder. Dragged media take its size and position, and new media replace the previous.
The number, names and order of the sheets and their content.
File > Save as Template, in the My Templates folder, which appears in the Chooser. Deleting the file deletes the template.

The window works on the minimum screen of 1280 × 720 and adapts to smaller windows, such as half a screen: sidebars and the Inspector become overlay panes, and the format bar collapses, as in Desk Writer. Phones and screens smaller than the minimum are not supported.
column8: Interface B: as in Desk Writer (GNM-01)

column4: Notices that need no answer appear in a toast, with Undo when the action can be undone.

column3: Unsaved documents at the end of the session
column4: With a changed and unsaved document, the app holds back the end of the session and shutdown until the person decides.
Sheets, tables, cells (with value, formula and headers), charts and objects appear in the accessibility tree, with role, name and description.
A thumbnailer shows the first sheet of .numbers and ODS documents in Files, without needing LibreOffice.
A LocalSearch extractor indexes the text and the information (author, title, keywords) of .numbers and ODS documents.
The GNOME Shell search lists the recent documents of the app and opens the chosen one in it.
Text in Hebrew, Persian and Arabic runs from right to left in cells, and the interface and the order of the columns mirror in these languages.
The interface is translated into the languages of po/LANGUAGES.md.

View and Insert in the title bar, Format at the end of the format bar, Arrange in the context menu, and the main menu with only file and application, as in Desk Writer (path B). A command search finds any item by name.
column8: Interface B: as in Desk Writer (GNM-10); Table becomes the context menu of the table and the Table tab of the Inspector
